resolutions.researcher_notes: Live URL (williams.com/2019/01/04/gulf-connector-project-placed-into-service/, from seed_citations) is a confirmed 404 today, so its Wayback capture is proposed instead per the blocked/dead-link rule (this is a genuine dead link on the live domain, but the Wayback capture is a full, readable copy — not a substitute for an unestablished-dead page, the page really is gone). The capture is Williams' own Jan 4, 2019 press release, headline 'Gulf Connector Project placed into service': 'The Gulf Connector Project expands the Transco pipeline's delivery capacity by 475 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d), providing service to Cheniere Energy's Corpus Christi liquefaction terminal and Freeport LNG Development, L.P.'s liquefaction project.' — an exact, direct match for Capacity=475.00 MMcf/d on the 'Gulf Connector Expansion' segment. Second, genuinely independent source: the Federal Register's Aug 31, 2016 FERC 'Notice of Application' for this same project (Docket No. CP16-494-000, published by the U.S. Government Publishing Office, i.e. a federal regulator's own notice, not Williams' filing or website): 'Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company, LLC (Transco) ... filed ... an application ... requesting authorization of its Gulf Connector Expansion Project ... [which] would enable 475,000 dekatherms per day of incremental firm natural gas transportation.' 475,000 Dth/d is the same figure as 475 MMcf/d — dekatherms and Mcf/d are used interchangeably for pipeline capacity in FERC filings and industry usage (both approximate 1 MMBtu of gas per unit), so this is the standard prose/unit-equivalence the brief permits, not a different number. Publishers are genuinely distinct (Williams Companies, a private corporation, vs. the U.S. Federal Register/FERC, an independent federal regulator) so independent:true and tier:high. Also checked but did NOT use: Cheniere Energy's own May 2018 8-K exhibits (SEC EDGAR full-text search, CIK 0000003570, d583086dex102.htm/dex103.htm) list a 'Precedent Agreement for Firm Transportation Service Under Gulf Connector Expansion Project, dated as of December 16, 2015, between CCL and Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company, LLC' — independently confirms this project and its parties are real, but states no capacity figure, so it is not proposed as a ref for this specific value (would be an orphan ref). ijglobal.com's transaction page for this project (also a seed citation) returned HTTP 403 (blocked, not deleted) with no Wayback capture available, so it was dropped rather than proposed. The nxtbook.com Pipeline & Gas Journal 'projects_august.html' seed citation returned HTTP 200 but is a JS flipbook-reader shell with no extractable text in this environment, so it could not be checked and was not used.
